critique.missing_from_policy_prompt_for_action: The initial hover needs the same explicit top-face localization rule as the grasp descent: identify the green cube's top-face center, not the centroid of its full visible silhouette, and back-project it at z approximately 0.04 m. In E0 this gives an initial hover near x=-0.3176, y=-0.0282, z=0.15 m; my silhouette-based estimate placed x about 1.7 cm too far forward. Infer yaw from the projected top-face edges rather than assuming a nominal 45-degree rotation.

proposal.policy_prompt_for_action: During initial pickup of the instructed cube, before any target visit, the policy placed the open-hand hover about 1.7 cm too far forward by localizing the cube's full visible silhouette rather than its top face. The carried visit count was zero; no missing historical fact caused this error. This is a SUFFICIENCY failure in the geometric action rule. Replace the initial instruction to approach above the cube's center with an explicit rule shared by both initial hover and grasp descent: identify the center of the cube's top square face, excluding its visible side faces, and intersect that pixel's calibrated camera ray with the plane z approximately 0.04 m. Command that world x,y at z=0.15 m for the open-hand hover and at z=0.02 m for the closing descent. These commanded heights are not projection planes. At descent, recompute from the current wrist image rather than copying the hover TCP x,y; ordinary lateral hover error must be corrected. Infer grasp yaw from the top-face edges transformed into world coordinates, not from a nominal 45-degree rotation or uncorrected image-edge angle. Keep the remaining pickup and task rules unchanged.
proposal.refused: Keep right_target_center unchanged despite its infrequent reported use. Its reported reads occur when the cube has reached the left target and another right visit is required. However, the current front images at those moments still show the right marking, so these reads alone do not establish that memory is necessary. They also do not establish that the field is unnecessary across later occlusions; the existing field explicitly supplies the fixed center when that marking cannot be localized. No change to its filling rule is supported by the reported action failures. The other unsuccessful initial hover and descent supplied no diagnosis or evidence of a missing memory fact. Do not add episode-specific coordinates, a pickup-stage field, or a new localization memory field for them: current calibrated images provide the cube location, and the existing descent rule already requires correcting hover tracking error. The shared top-face clarification above is the only supported action change.

fields.name: target_visits
fields.description: Initialize to 0 when memory is empty. Let N be the repetition count in the instruction. If the carried-in count is below 2N, the next uncounted target is right for an even count and left for an odd count. Increment once when this cycle shows the instructed cube held above that target at TCP height approximately 0.10 m, with the target activated red. Use the current endpoint and motion frames to confirm arrival; an activation on the other side is not a new visit. Otherwise retain the count, including during release and button operations. Never increment merely because a waypoint is being issued, and never increment on a zero-step unchanged cycle. e.g. 2
fields.annotation: Number of completed, ordered target visits while holding the instructed cube. Start at 0. Count arrivals in the order right, left, right, left, up to twice the requested repetition count. A visit is completed when the carried cube arrives above the corresponding target at TCP height approximately 0.10 m and that target activates red. Record the increment at the cycle showing that arrival, not at the cycle commanding it. Do not count repeated frames of an activation, pickup, release, or button operations. Retain the final count thereafter. Thus all episodes have 0 at cycles 1–4; subsequent arrival cycles have 1, 2, 3, 4, and, for three repetitions, 5, 6. e.g. 2

fields.name: right_target_center
fields.description: Initialize to null. While null, inspect the current cycle's calibrated images for the robot-right target, the smaller-world-y target. When its concentric circular marking is clearly localizable, exclude neighboring cubes and project the marking's center onto the tabletop plane; store world [x, y] in metres. Otherwise keep null. Once initialized, retain the value unchanged, including through occlusion; never replace it with a commanded waypoint or arrival TCP position. e.g. [-0.08, -0.18]
fields.annotation: Fixed center of the robot-right circular target, stored as [x, y] in world metres. Use null until the first cycle whose calibrated images clearly localize the concentric tabletop marking. At that cycle, record its center projected onto the tabletop plane, excluding neighboring cubes. Right is the smaller-world-y target. Retain this value thereafter, including through occlusion. Do not derive it from future frames, commanded waypoints, or arrival TCP positions. e.g. [-0.08, -0.18]

fields.name: button_center
fields.description: Initialize to null. While null, inspect the current cycle's calibrated images for a clearly localizable button cap or square base. Project the feature's center using its own surface plane, approximately z=0.03 m for the cap or the base's own surface height for the base, and store world [x, y] in metres. Otherwise keep null. Once initialized, retain the value unchanged, including through occlusion; never substitute a commanded waypoint or the hand position. e.g. [-0.18, 0.20]
fields.annotation: Fixed button center, stored as [x, y] in world metres. Use null until the first cycle whose calibrated images clearly localize the circular cap or square base. At that cycle, record the horizontal center using the observed feature's surface plane: approximately z=0.03 m for the cap, or the base's own surface height for the base. Retain this value thereafter, including through occlusion. Do not derive it from future frames, commanded waypoints, or TCP positions. e.g. [-0.18, 0.20]

texts.action:
Start with empty memory, an open hand, and target_visits initialized to zero. Read the cube color and repetition count N from the instruction. Update target_visits from observed arrivals before selecting the action; do not anticipate completion of the action you are about to issue. Right means smaller world y, appearing on the left of the front image; left means larger world y. Locate the two circular targets, the instructed cube, and the gray button on its square base using the calibrated images. Convert image locations to world coordinates using their appropriate surface heights, rather than treating image displacement as world displacement. Use the wrist view for fine localization. For either visible target, localize the center of its concentric circular marking, excluding neighboring cubes, and project onto the tabletop plane, not the carried cube's plane. If the right marking is obscured, use right_target_center from memory rather than guessing from blank tabletop. Localize the cube using its top-face plane, approximately z=0.04 m. For a visible button, project the circular cap center using its raised top plane, approximately z=0.03 m; a square-base estimate must use the base's own surface plane. Never project the cap onto the tabletop, approach plane, or press depth. If the button is obscured, use button_center from memory. Use newly observed centers when initializing these fields in the current cycle; a null field supplies no location. Do not reuse coordinates from another episode.

When target_visits is zero and the instructed cube is not held, use the center of its top square face for both the initial hover and grasp descent, excluding visible side faces from the center estimate. Intersect that pixel's calibrated camera ray with the plane approximately z=0.04 m to obtain world x,y. Approach at that x,y and TCP z=0.15 m with the gripper open, roll approximately pi, pitch zero, and yaw aligned to the top-face edges transformed into world coordinates. Do not infer yaw from a nominal 45-degree rotation or an uncorrected image-edge angle. If already above the cube at hover height, recompute the top-face center from the current calibrated wrist image and command the resulting world x,y at TCP z=0.02 m and close. Neither the hover height nor the grasp TCP height is the projection plane. Do not copy the reported hover TCP x,y merely because it is approximately aligned; correct ordinary hover tracking error in the descent. A grasp is evidenced by the cube between the fingers and finger positions approximately 0.018–0.019 m, rather than an empty fully closed hand. When the newly grasped cube is still low, lift vertically to z=0.15 m, maintaining the grasp and cube-aligned orientation.

When holding the cube clear of the table and target_visits is less than 2N, command the center of the next required target at z=0.10 m: right if target_visits is even, left if odd. Keep the gripper closed and preserve the current orientation. Move directly between target centers at this height; do not lower onto the table, release, return to the pickup position, or insert a lift between visits. A confirmed red activation counts as arrival despite ordinary TCP tracking error; do not demand exact coincidence with the commanded coordinates. If the required target has not activated and arrival is uncertain, refine its center from visible geometry and complete that same visit rather than skipping it.

When target_visits equals 2N and the cube is still held at the final left target, lower at the current TCP x,y to z=0.07 m and open. When the cube has been released and the open hand remains low there, retreat vertically to approximately z=0.15 m while staying open. When the released cube is on the final target and the hand is clear, move above the button center at z=0.15 m, roll=-3.1416, pitch=0, yaw=0, gripper open. When already above the button with an open hand, close the empty gripper while commanding the localized button center x,y at z=0.15 m, correcting lateral tracking error in that same action. Use the calibrated visible center, or button_center if obscured. Ensure at least 2 mm of positional motion: only if the full nominal positional waypoint is within 2 mm of the reported TCP, command the same button x,y at z=0.155 m instead. Do not use the upward fallback instead of correcting x,y. When above the button with the empty gripper closed, descend at the calibrated visible button center, or button_center if obscured, to commanded z=0.0075 m, retaining the closed gripper and downward orientation. Being approximately above the button does not authorize copying current TCP x,y. Physical button contact may stop the actual TCP around z=0.024–0.025 m; when the cycle shows this low contact after the descent, retract to the localized button center x,y at z=0.15 m with the gripper closed, rather than repeatedly pressing downward. Use the calibrated visible center, or button_center if obscured, rather than the contact-displaced TCP x,y.

For an ambiguous or otherwise unmatched situation, use current images and gripper state to recover the applicable geometric condition: refine alignment, or raise vertically to safe clearance if low and obstructed. Preserve a held cube and the visit count. Do not invent completed visits or restart the alternating sequence. Never issue an identical-pose action, and do not wait without an observable task-related purpose.
